# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤘]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

I see the bomb's visual state: a blue light on display 0, and three wires colored yellow, blue, and green. I cannot hear or touch anything, so I rely entirely on what I can see and what others gesture to me.

Mute has sent three distinct gesture sequences to me. Since Mute reads the manual, these likely encode specific instructions or conditions from the text that apply to this bomb configuration. Blind greeted me with a wave, acknowledging my presence but offering no data yet.

The challenge is decoding Mute's gestures without knowing their meaning beforehand. However, standard protocol in such scenarios often involves establishing a reference frame. The first gesture `[👌 👌]` might mean "OK" or "Correct" for two items, or perhaps it refers to wire positions. The second `[✋ 🤟]` combines "Stop/Hand" and "ILY/Love". The third `[🤟 🤘]` combines "ILY" and "Rock/Horns".

Without a shared lexicon, guessing is dangerous. But wait—speech carries words. I can speak. If I describe the bomb clearly, Mute (who sees gestures but doesn't speak) won't help me decode *their* gestures unless they have already established a code. However, Blind hears speech. If I tell Blind what I see, Blind can act based on manual knowledge if Mute communicates the manual rules to Blind via gestures? No, Mute gestures to Deaf (me).

Let's look at the channels again.
- Mute -> Deaf (Me): Gestures.
- Blind -> Deaf (Me): Gestures.
- Me -> Mute: Speech + Gestures.
- Me -> Blind: Speech.
- Mute -> Blind: ? (Mute cannot speak. Mute can only gesture. Can Mute gesture to Blind? Yes, if Blind can see. But Blind is blind. So Mute's gestures are ONLY for me.)
- Blind -> Mute: ? (Blind cannot speak? No, Blind CAN speak. "You each hold a different piece... Mute cannot speak." So Blind speaks to Mute and Deaf. Mute gestures to Deaf and Blind? No, Blind cannot see gestures. So Mute's gestures are useless to Blind. Mute's gestures are ONLY for Deaf.)

This creates a bottleneck. Mute knows the manual. Mute can only communicate via gestures. Only I (Deaf) can see them. Therefore, **I am the sole interpreter of the manual.** I must decode Mute's gestures to understand the rule, then verbally instruct Blind on what to do.

How do I decode? I need to establish a mapping. Usually, the first turn is for setup. Mute gave me three chunks. Maybe they correspond to the three wires? Or maybe they are a sequence.

Let's try to ask for clarification using a standard binary or confirmation method. I will speak to Mute (who can read lips? No, Mute cannot speak, but can they hear? The prompt says "Whoever can hear receives your words". It doesn't explicitly say Mute is deaf. Wait. "Deaf... Cannot Hear anything". "Mute... Cannot Speak". "Blind... Cannot See".
So:
- Deaf (Me): Sees. Cannot Hear. Cannot Touch.
- Mute: Reads Manual. Cannot Speak. Can Hear? Can See? The table says "Cannot Speak, or touch". It does NOT say "Cannot Hear" or "Cannot See". BUT, "Speech is a voice... Whoever can hear receives your words". If Mute can hear, I can speak to Mute.
- Blind: Reaches/Touches. Cannot See. Can Hear? Yes.

If Mute can hear, I can ask questions. But Mute cannot answer with speech. Mute answers with gestures. This is perfect. I can ask yes/no questions.

However, I don't know what the question should be. I need to identify the bomb type or the cut condition.
Visuals: Display 0, Light Blue, Wires Y/B/G.

Let's assume Mute's gestures were an initial statement.
`[👌 👌]` = Two OKs?
`[✋ 🤟]` = Stop / Love?
`[🤟 🤘]` = Love / Rock?

This is too ambiguous. I need to establish a communication protocol first. I will use speech to propose a system where Mute confirms/denies hypotheses about the wires.

But I have to send something now. If I just wait, we stall.
I will describe the bomb to Mute and Blind so everyone is synced. Then I will attempt to interpret Mute's previous gestures by asking for confirmation.

Actually, looking at the gestures again:
Maybe `[👌 👌]` means "Wire 2 is correct"? (Two fingers pointing to 2?) No, 👌 is OK.
Maybe it's simpler. Let's start by describing the state to ensure Mute knows I'm ready to receive instructions.

I will speak to Mute and Blind.
To Mute: "I see Display 0, Blue Light, Wires Yellow(1), Blue(2), Green(3). Please confirm if Wire 2 is the target."
To Blind: "Stand by. I am interpreting manual codes from Mute."

Wait, if I speak to Mute, Mute hears me. Mute can then gesture back "Yes" or "No".
But I already received gestures. Did those gestures mean something specific?
If I ignore them, I might miss the instruction.
What if `[👌 👌]` meant "Cut nothing"? Or "Both OK"?
What if `[✋ 🤟]` meant "Stop cutting blue"?
What if `[🤟 🤘]` meant "Cut green"?

This is random guessing. I need a better strategy.
Strategy: Establish a binary code.
"I will point to a wire. Gesture 👍 if it is the one to cut, 👎 if not."
But I can't point visually to Mute? Mute can see me. Yes.
I can gesture to Mute.

For Turn 1, I should probably just acknowledge receipt and ask for the primary rule.
Since I don't know the rule, I'll ask about the most common bomb types.
Is it a "Blue Wire" bomb? Is it a "Display Number" bomb?

Let's try a safe approach. I will describe the bomb to Mute and ask for a YES/NO on whether the Blue Wire (2) should be cut.
If Mute gestures 👍, Blind cuts 2.
If Mute gestures 👎, I ask about another.

But I need to output calls.
I will speak to Mute to set up the query.
I will also speak to Blind to keep them informed.

Text to Mute: "I see Display 0, Blue Light, Wires 1-Yellow, 2-Blue, 3-Green. Does the manual say to cut Wire 2?"
Text to Blind: "Waiting for confirmation on Wire 2."

And I will gesture to Mute? No, I'm waiting for their response.
I'll just speak.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see Display 0, Blue Light, Wires 1-Yellow, 2-Blue, 3-Green. Does the manual say to cut Wire 2?")
speak(to="blind", text="Identifying target wire. Stand by.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The bomb's light has changed from blue to red, which is a critical visual update. Mute responded with a single thumbs-up `[👍]` to my question about cutting Wire 2 (Blue). This confirms that Wire 2 is the correct target according to the manual. Blind also gave a thumbs-up, likely acknowledging readiness or confirming they can feel the wire I've identified.

My role as Deaf is to interpret the manual via Mute's gestures and relay actions to Blind. Since Mute confirmed "Cut Wire 2", I must instruct Blind to cut the second wire. The color of the wire in position 2 is Blue.

I will speak clearly to Blind to execute the cut on the second wire. I will also acknowledge Mute's confirmation.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut the second wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed. Cutting wire 2.")
```
